text: About 4,000 years ago, farming with maize, beans and squash spread through southern Mexico and Guatemala.
The Maya were many peoples and kingdoms with related languages, never one single nation.
src: Archaeologists date the beginning of the Preclassic period to about 2000 BCE, when farming based on maize, beans and squash was spreading through the region / south-eastern Mexico ... Guatemala, Belize
The Maya were never a single nation or empire but many peoples and kingdoms who spoke related Mayan languages and shared a common culture

text: In time they built great cities, with temples and platforms rising above the forest.
src: Nakbe had large platforms and temples by about 800 BCE / temple-pyramids rising from the forest

text: Kings were called “holy lords”, and royal women such as Lady Six Sky could hold power.
Most people were farmers who lived in houses of poles and thatch.
src: each ruled by a k’uhul ajaw, a “holy lord” / royal women could hold power, as Lady Six Sky did at Naranjo in the late 7th century
the farming families who made up most of the population and lived in houses of poles and thatch on low platforms

text: They worshipped many gods, like Itzamna, an old creator god of the sky and writing.
Kings offered their own blood, and captives taken in war were often killed as offerings.
src: Among their gods were Itzamna, an aged creator associated with the sky and with writing
They let their own blood as offerings / Rulers raided rival cities to take captives, who were displayed, humiliated and often sacrificed

text: Maya scribes made the most complete writing system of the ancient Americas, and kept careful calendars.
King Pakal of Palenque was buried inside this temple.
src: Maya scribes developed the most complete writing system of the ancient Americas / With it scribes kept several calendars at once
Palenque’s Temple of the Inscriptions held the tomb of Pakal

text: The Spanish conquered the Maya kingdoms, and a Spanish friar burned many Maya books.
Maya writers kept their histories in books like these, and over six million Maya live today.
src: The Spanish conquest was slow and fiercely resisted / in 1562 Diego de Landa burned Maya books and images at Maní
Using the Latin alphabet, they wrote down their histories and sacred traditions in works such as the Popol Vuh, the Books of Chilam Balam / Today well over six million people are Maya
